I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best and can still manage at my age. I will mainly do the usual winter wheat followed by summer maize rotation, because it fits our land, our water conditions, our machinery, and my experience. I only finished primary school, so I do not want a complicated planting plan with too many crops or too much fine management. I will keep things simple, stable, and familiar. Wheat gives me a dependable winter crop, and maize follows well after harvest. This rotation also spreads labor over the year better than trying to handle vegetables or other higher-risk cash crops.

I will use improved or hybrid seed rather than old saved seed, because I want more even emergence and a steadier yield. I will not push fertilizer too aggressively, because inputs cost money and I am old enough to value stability over chasing the highest output. I will still apply nitrogen as the main fertilizer, with phosphorus and potassium at moderate levels so the crop does not become too weak or overly dependent on nitrogen alone. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and lighter for me to manage than deep ploughing on all the land. For irrigation, I will water wheat more than maize, since wheat in our area usually needs more support through winter-spring growth, while maize can often rely more on summer rain unless the season turns dry. I will spray pesticides only as needed but I will still plan for a few applications, because I do not want weeds, aphids, armyworm, rust, or other common problems to get ahead of me. My goal is not the most ambitious plan. My goal is a practical plan I can actually carry through.
